name: Opening range breakout on stocks in play (5-minute ORB)

origin.source_title: A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market (SSRN 4729284; Swiss Finance Institute Research Paper 24-98)

how_it_works.simple: Watch only the stocks with unusual trading that morning, usually because of news. If the first five minutes close up, buy; if down, sell short; get out by the close.
how_it_works.analogy: Like joining the crowd that has already started running, but only on days when there is a real reason to run.
how_it_works.precise: Stocks in play are screened by relative volume (opening price above $5, average volume of at least 1 million shares over 14 days, 14-day ATR above $0.50, per one summary). Trade in the direction of the first 5-minute candle, with a stop sized from ATR, and close at the end of the day. The paper holds the top 20 stocks by relative volume each day.

rule: Each day, rank liquid US stocks by opening relative volume and take the top 20. Go long if the first 5-minute bar closes above its open, short if below; stop-loss sized from the 14-day ATR (the exact fraction is in the paper, which we have not read); exit at the close.
economic_rationale: News days bring informed order flow and attention, so the opening move tends to continue during the day for stocks with real news.
why_it_might_fail: One of the authors sells day-trading education, and the paper's 2016 to 2023 sample is short. Intraday costs and short-sale constraints on news stocks are hard to model, and later costs could take most of the edge.

reported_results.market: US stocks, top 20 stocks in play
reported_results.notes: Abstract: a portfolio of the top 20 stocks in play achieved total net performance of over 1,600%, a Sharpe ratio of 2.81 and an annualised alpha of 36%, against 198% for the S&P 500. The abstract says this holds after transaction costs but does not state the assumptions.

implementations.notes: QuantConnect replication; its own reported Sharpe is about 2.4 (from a search summary, not read by us).

relevance.reason: Opening range breakouts are among the most taught and botted day-trading rules, so a published, costed version gives Verify a reference point for day-trader logs.

research.notes: Needs intraday bars for thousands of stocks, which we do not have free. Added by Amanda's library batch on 2026-10-25 (options, intraday and equity anomalies that retail traders and bots claim to use).
